body_markdown:
Blog


September 17, 2026


Alvah Bickner


Quindar v0.38 introduces a set of practical updates designed to make day-to-day mission workflows clearer, more precise, and easier to manage.


This release strengthens several parts of the operator experience, from fleet planning and contact scheduling to asset-level visibility and flight dynamics configuration. It also includes documentation improvements that make core workflows easier to understand and navigate.


Together, these updates reinforce what mission teams need most from mission management software: a common operating picture, better operational clarity, and more control over mission-critical decisions.


## Enhanced Ground Station Management


Ground stations and space-ground links can now be enabled or disabled directly in the Quindar platform.


That gives teams a more practical way to control which resources are considered during scheduling. When a ground station is disabled, it is automatically removed from scheduling considerations, helping operators reduce noise and keep planning aligned with current mission needs.


For teams managing complex networks of providers, assets, and links, that added control supports a more intentional and mission-ready scheduling workflow.


## More Context in Upcoming Contacts


Quindar now displays the ground station provider in the Upcoming Contacts table.


This gives operators clearer visibility into which provider is fulfilling a request and adds an extra layer of confidence when reviewing or canceling scheduled contacts. Small context improvements like this matter in operational environments, where faster understanding leads to faster and more confident decisions.


## More Precise Fleet Planning Filters


The Fleet Planning experience now gives operators more precise ways to focus on the contacts and assets that matter most. In addition to adding timeline filters for Asset Status and Operational Mode, these filters will use an “Or” argument to ensure operators can surface the right subset of assets without overly restricting the dashboard view.


Together, these updates make it easier to move from a broad fleet view to the exact operational slice teams need. Operators can narrow the timeline to the right subset of assets and filter contact data based on real-time planning needs without losing context in the middle of an operation.


## Cleaner Asset-Level Runbook Visibility


On the Asset page, the runbooks widget now shows only runbooks created for or run against the current asset.


This update reduces distraction and helps operators focus on the workflows that are actually relevant to the asset in view. At the same time, teams still retain access to any available runbook when they want to initiate a new action.


## New Collision Avoidance Ticketing Control


v0.38 also adds a new front-end toggle that determines whether a ticket should automatically be created when a new CDM is received.


This gives teams more explicit control over how collision avoidance workflows are managed, helping them align ticketing behavior with their operational posture. In environments where speed, oversight, and automation all need to work together, that flexibility matters.


## Documentation Updates That Support Faster Feature Adoption


This release also includes meaningful documentation updates across the platform.


[New documentation pages](https://docs.quindar.space/) were added for core areas including Fleet Planning, File Transfer, Task Definitions, Contact Profiles, Scheduled Jobs, Ground Stations, Ground Targets, Partner Sharing, and Quindar Assistant. A dedicated Quindar Portal section was also introduced, along with reorganized documentation for areas like Flight Dynamics and Fleet Operations.


These updates make product knowledge easier to find and easier to follow, helping both existing operators and newer users get to the right information faster.
